subject: Physics
title: Electromagnetic Induction
summary: Whenever the magnetic flux Φ = B·A through a coil changes, an emf is induced in it (Faraday). Flux can change in three ways: B changes, area changes (a sliding rod), or angle changes (a rotating coil — generator).
The induced current always flows so as to oppose the CHANGE in flux (Lenz's law) — a direct consequence of energy conservation. Hence the minus sign: ε = −N dΦ/dt.
A coil opposes changes in its own current — self inductance L (ε = −L dI/dt) — and induces emf in a nearby coil — mutual inductance M. An inductor stores energy ½LI² in its magnetic field.
Changing flux in a piece of metal sets up circulating eddy currents — useful in braking and induction furnaces, wasteful in transformer cores (hence laminated cores).

formulas.name: Magnetic flux
formulas.formula: Φ = B·A = BA cos θ;   N turns: NΦ (flux linkage);   unit weber (T·m²)
formulas.when: How much field passes through a coil.
formulas.mistake: θ is between B and the NORMAL to the area, not the plane of the coil.

formulas.name: Faraday's law
formulas.note: Large flux doesn't give emf — CHANGING flux does.

formulas.name: Lenz's law
formulas.formula: The induced current opposes the change in flux (minus sign)
formulas.mistake: It opposes the CHANGE in flux, not the flux — if flux increases the induced field is opposite; if flux decreases it is in the same direction.

formulas.name: Charge through the coil
formulas.when: Total charge that flows (no time needed).
formulas.note: It doesn't depend on how fast the flux changed.

formulas.name: Motional emf (rod)
formulas.formula: ε = Blv  (B, l, v mutually perpendicular);   general: ε = (v × B)·l
formulas.note: If they aren't perpendicular, use only the perpendicular components.

formulas.name: Rod on rails with resistance
formulas.formula: I = Blv/R;   magnetic drag F = B²l²v/R;   power = F v = B²l²v²/R
formulas.note: Drag is proportional to velocity — that's why a terminal velocity appears.

formulas.name: Rotating rod
formulas.formula: ε = ½Bωl²  (rod rotating about one end)
formulas.note: This is between the two ends; with a central pivot the two halves' emfs cancel.

formulas.name: AC generator emf
formulas.formula: ε = NBAω sin ωt;   peak ε₀ = NBAω
formulas.note: ω = 2πf in rad/s; convert rpm first.

formulas.name: Self inductance
formulas.formula: NΦ = LI;   ε = −L dI/dt;   unit henry
formulas.note: L comes from geometry; it doesn't depend on the current.

formulas.name: Inductance of a solenoid
formulas.formula: L = μ₀μ_r N²A / l = μ₀μ_r n² A l
formulas.note: Goes as N² — doubling the turns makes L four times.

formulas.name: Mutual inductance
formulas.formula: N₂Φ₂ = M I₁;   ε₂ = −M dI₁/dt;   co-axial solenoids: M = μ₀ n₁ N₂ A;   M ≤ √(L₁L₂)
formulas.note: M is the same for both coils (M₁₂ = M₂₁).

formulas.name: Energy stored in an inductor
formulas.formula: U = ½LI²;   energy density u = B²/2μ₀
formulas.mistake: It goes as current squared — don't compute it from voltage directly.

formulas.name: LR circuit (growth and decay)
formulas.formula: Growth: I = (E/R)(1 − e^{−t/τ});  decay: I = I₀e^{−t/τ};  τ = L/R
formulas.mistake: At t = τ the current is 63% of its final value, not 50%.

examples.title: Faraday: average emf
examples.problem: Flux per turn through a 100-turn coil falls from 0.02 Wb to 0.005 Wb in 0.1 s. emf?
examples.solution: ε = NΔΦ/Δt = 100 × 0.015/0.1 = 15 V. Flux is decreasing ⇒ the induced current makes a field in the same direction (Lenz).

examples.title: Rod on rails
examples.problem: A 0.5 m rod slides at 4 m/s in B = 0.3 T; circuit resistance R = 2 Ω. emf, current, drag force, power?

examples.title: Rotating rod
examples.problem: A 1 m rod rotates about one end at 20 rad/s in B = 0.5 T parallel to the axis. emf?

examples.title: L of a solenoid
examples.problem: 500 turns, length 0.5 m, area 10⁻³ m² (air core). L?

examples.title: Self-induced emf and energy
examples.problem: Current in L = 0.2 H falls from 5 A to 0 in 0.01 s. emf? Energy stored at 5 A?
examples.solution: ε = L ΔI/Δt = 0.2 × 5/0.01 = 100 V (hence the spark at the switch). U = ½LI² = ½ × 0.2 × 25 = 2.5 J.

examples.title: Mutual induction
examples.problem: M = 0.05 H; primary current changes at 40 A/s. emf in the secondary?

examples.title: Peak emf of a generator
examples.problem: 100 turns, area 0.01 m², B = 0.5 T, coil turns at 50 rev/s. Peak emf?

examples.title: Charge that flows
examples.problem: A 10-turn coil of R = 5 Ω has its flux per turn of 0.02 Wb removed completely. Charge that flows?
examples.solution: Q = NΔΦ/R = 10 × 0.02/5 = 0.04 C — whether removed quickly or slowly.

examples.title: LR circuit
examples.problem: L = 2 H, R = 4 Ω, battery 12 V. Time constant, final current and current at t = τ?

examples.title: M of two solenoids
examples.problem: A long solenoid has 1000 turns/m; inside it is a small 100-turn coil of area 2 × 10⁻⁴ m². M?

topics.title: Experiments of Faraday and Henry
topics.explain: (1) Move a magnet towards/away from a coil — the galvanometer deflects; when the magnet stops, zero. (2) Switch the current in a nearby coil on/off — current in the other coil. (3) Rotate a coil in a field. Common idea: changing flux gives emf.

topics.title: Lenz's law and energy
topics.explain: Bring a magnet's north pole towards a coil and the near face of the coil becomes north, pushing the magnet away — work is needed to push it in, and that work becomes electrical energy. If the current helped the motion we would get free energy — impossible.

topics.title: How motional emf arises
topics.explain: Electrons in the rod feel a force qvB pushing them to one end — the rod becomes a battery. With a closed circuit a current flows, and the current feels a drag force BIl opposing the motion.

topics.title: Eddy currents
topics.explain: Changing flux sets up circulating currents in metal plates/cores. Uses: electromagnetic brakes (trains), induction furnaces, induction cooktops, damping in galvanometers, speedometers. Drawback: heating and energy loss — so transformer and motor cores are laminated (thin insulated sheets).

topics.title: Self induction
topics.explain: A coil behaves like electrical inertia: it resists changes in current. Opening a switch makes the current fall suddenly ⇒ large emf ⇒ spark. A choke coil reduces AC current without wasting energy.

topics.title: Mutual induction
topics.explain: A changing current in one coil induces emf in another. M depends on distance, orientation and core; closer and coaxial coils give larger M. Transformers and wireless chargers work on this.

topics.title: AC generator
topics.explain: A coil rotates in uniform B, Φ = NBA cos ωt ⇒ ε = NBAω sin ωt. Slip rings and brushes take out AC. Mechanical energy (turbine) → electrical energy.

ratta: ε = −N dΦ/dt;  Φ = BA cos θ.
Rod: ε = Blv;  rotating rod: ½Bωl².
